chunks: It was not you who killed them, but God did so. You did not throw what you threw, (sand into the eyes of the enemy at Badr), but God, to bring out the best in the faithful by doing them a favour of His own. God is all-hearing and all-knowing.
ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of 'You did not throw when you threw' in the context of the Battle of Badr?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse highlights the distinction between human effort (asbab) and divine causality (sabab), affirming that the Prophet’s physical action of throwing sand was the means, while God’s will was the true agent of victory. It underscores the concept of 'bala' hasan' (a good trial), indicating that the believers' faith was refined through this divine intervention, reinforcing their reliance on God rather than mere military prowess.
